additions.reason: The Torah explicitly equates ראות (sight/vision) with השגחה. The Talmudic source cited (Shabbat 151b) teaches that sight follows weeping — the tears take the faculty of sight into themselves. The Rebbe concludes from this that tears carry 'portions of hashgacha and sight' (חֶלְקֵי הַהַשְׁגָּחָה וְהָרְאוּת). ראות is thus a bechina of השגחה, closely paralleling the eye as the instrument of divine oversight. It belongs in Package 1 alongside דמעות and השגחה.
additions.source_quote: נִמְצָא, שֶׁהַדְּמָעוֹת הֵם חֶלְקֵי הַהַשְׁגָּחָה וְהָרְאוּת, כִּי הַדְּמָעוֹת לוֹקְחִים הָרְאוּת כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: In the proof text of edge 609, the Rebbe explicitly writes that prayer 'is a bechina of miracles and hashgacha' (תְּפִלָּה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת נִסִּים וְהַשְׁגָּחָה הֶפֶךְ הַטֶּבַע). Miracles are grouped here as the same essential domain as hashgacha — both are the opposite of nature. This node should be added to Package 1.
additions.source_quote: נִמְצָא שֶׁתְּפִלָּה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת נִסִּים וְהַשְׁגָּחָה הֶפֶךְ הַטֶּבַע, הִיא בְּחִינַת גָּדוֹל

additions.reason: The Torah explicitly identifies ים הגדול (the Great Sea) as a bechina of the nations (עכו"ם) who rule over Israel: 'לַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל – הַיְנוּ בְּחִינוֹת הָעַכּוּ"ם הַמּוֹשְׁלִין עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.' This is a bechina statement connecting the metaphor of the sea to the oppressive nations. However, there is only one bechina pair here (ים הגדול = עכו"ם), insufficient to form a standalone package. It is flagged as a missing node. If a future evil-domain package is built for this Torah, ים הגדול and עכו"ם would anchor it alongside הטבע and מזל.
additions.source_quote: לַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל – הַיְנוּ בְּחִינוֹת הָעַכּוּ"ם הַמּוֹשְׁלִין עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, בְּחִינַת (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ נ"ז): וְהָרְשָׁעִים כַּיָּם נִגְרָשׁ

Both are bechina edges and both are correctly assigned to Package 1. This is expected behavior for a symmetric bechina relationship that was encoded twice in the dataset.
concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: ראות (sight/vision) — explicitly called a bechina of hashgacha via the tears mechanism
נסים (miracles) — grouped as bechina of hashgacha in edge 609 proof text
ים הגדול (the Great Sea) — called a bechina of the oppressing nations (עכו"ם)

דעת (knowledge/awareness) — the theological root of the entire Torah; all suffering stems from חסרון הדעת. Daat is the condition for hashgacha to be felt. However, in this Torah daat is presented as a prerequisite (eitza relationship) rather than as a bechina-equivalent of hashgacha itself.
טבע/מזל (nature/fate) — the opposite domain to hashgacha; not a bechina of any good concept but structurally the anti-hashgacha. Appears only in eitza contexts in the dataset.
analysis_notes.structural_observation: Torah #250 is a short, concentrated teaching with a single dense conceptual cluster. The Rebbe draws one sustained bechina chain: prayer = hashgacha = greatness, and tears = hashgacha. The entire Torah revolves around this one package. The evil/natural domain (טבע, מזל, עכו"ם) is present as the backdrop but never formalized into bechina equivalences in the dataset.
